The course cluster looks and behaves like a real Alliance cluster. A few
concepts before you run anything.

## Login vs. compute nodes

- **Login node** — where you land when you connect. Use it only for light work:
  editing files, moving data, launching jobs. **Never run heavy computations on
  the login node.**
- **Compute nodes** — where real work runs. You don't use them directly; you
  **request** them through the **Slurm** scheduler, which queues your request and
  runs it when resources are free. The [JupyterLab](jupyterlab.qmd) portal does
  this for you automatically.

## Storage

| Space | Path | Use it for | Notes |
|-------|------|-----------|-------|
| Home | `/home/$USER` | code, scripts, small files | your personal space |
| Scratch | `/scratch/$USER` | large temporary run data | for big / short-lived files |
| Project | `/project` | shared course data | read the tutorial data from here |

::: {.callout-warning}
## Nothing here is permanent
This is a disposable training cluster — **all storage is wiped when the instance
is torn down at the end of the course.** Download anything you want to keep.
:::

## Software

Software is provided through **environment modules**, exactly as on the national
clusters:

```bash
module avail             # list available software
module load python/3.11  # load a specific version
```

Inside JupyterLab the Python environment is already set up for you.
